quizzes.stem: A team commits `.mcp.json` with the header `Bearer ${NPM_TOKEN}` for a hosted package registry. Every developer exports the variable, yet the registry answers 401. What is the cause?

options.a: Claude Code sends nothing for names that carry sign-in secrets of this kind
options.b: Header values are expanded only for entries that start a local process
options.c: The file loads only after an interactive approval that the developers skipped
options.d: A variable in a header needs a fallback after the dash and colon before use

explanation.a: Credential names such as this one read as empty toward a remote endpoint.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a server that waits for approval is not connected at all: "claude mcp list shows it as pending", and it does not answer with a 401.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the documentation lists the places where expansion applies: "`headers`: for HTTP server authentication".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a default is optional, and the plain form works: "expands to the value of environment variable".

quizzes.stem: A developer needs an integration that signs in with a personal account's token. It should exist in this repository only, and the token must never reach teammates through version control. Where should it be registered?

options.a: User scope, kept in the home directory file
options.b: Project scope, kept in the shared `.mcp.json` file
options.c: Local scope, the default for a newly added server
options.d: The local settings file, kept inside the repository

explanation.c: Local scope is the default and belongs to its owner and that one project. The guide names user-level scope for personal servers, and the product has a third scope between the two, which is the one that fits a single repository.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Selecting the wrong scope for a personal tool can leak credentials into a shared repo".
explanation.a: Ruled out because user scope is for "services you frequently use across different projects", which is wider than this repository.
explanation.d: Ruled out because that file holds settings and not servers: "while the general local settings file is `.claude/settings.local.json` in the project".

quizzes.stem: An agent keeps answering documentation questions with Grep on the checkout, although the team's documentation server has a search tool whose description reads `Searches docs`. What is the best fix?

options.a: Make the documentation server load at the start so the definition is visible
options.b: Lengthen the description past the cut-off so that no detail is left out
options.c: Remove the competing tool so that only the documentation tool remains
options.d: Say when it beats pattern matching and what comes back, main point first

explanation.d: The description is what the model chooses by, so it must say when to prefer the tool, with the point first.
explanation.a: Ruled out because loading at the start only makes the definition visible: "makes the definition visible and does not say when to prefer it".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Removing Grep is a blunt answer, because the agent then cannot search the code in the checkout".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Claude Code truncates each tool description and each server's instructions at 2,048 characters by default".

quizzes.stem: A support agent calls three listing tools before each database question, only to learn which tables exist. Which change cuts those calls?

options.a: Raise the output limit so that each listing returns more rows at once
options.b: Attach the schemas as a resource that can be mentioned in the prompt
options.c: Mark the listing tools as read-only so that they can run side by side
options.d: Move the database server into the user scope so that it loads everywhere

explanation.b: A catalog is wanted before work starts, and a resource can be attached to the prompt so that no discovery calls are needed.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "The limit concerns the size of one result and does nothing for the number of calls".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a hint "does not change this: it describes the tool to a client and does not tell the model what exists".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "it decides where a server loads and not what it exposes".

quizzes.stem: A team gives the agent its whole orders database through one MCP tool that runs any SQL it is given, and the job is to report on open orders. What is the architectural concern?

options.a: A result above the limit is lost, so the agent never sees the rows
options.b: The description is cut at the limit, so the agent cannot use it
options.c: Tool search hides the definition until a person asks for it
options.d: Access cannot be narrowed, because one entry point covers every task

explanation.d: A permission rule can allow or deny a tool by name, so one tool that does everything leaves nothing to scope.
explanation.a: Ruled out because an oversized result is kept: "Claude Code saves it to a file and replaces it in the conversation with a message that names the file path".
explanation.b: Ruled out because truncation is handled by wording: "put critical details near the start".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a definition is found by the model and not by a person: "a definition is loaded when Claude needs it".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4, a developer-productivity agent. The agent explores unfamiliar codebases with the built-in tools and several MCP servers. A team's shared `.mcp.json` starts a documentation server with the argument `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/tools/docs_server.py`, and on every machine the server fails to start with that text unexpanded in the path. What should the entry say?

options.a: A fallback after the name, written with a colon and a dash
options.b: An absolute location from the lead developer's own checkout, fixed for all
options.c: The same line placed in the user-level file, where the name is set
options.d: The name moved into the `env` map so that the process receives it

explanation.a: The variable is set for the server and not for Claude Code, so a path in `command` or `args` needs a fallback.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the text in `args` would still have nothing to expand from: "so `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` in a project file has nothing to expand from".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a personal location fails on every other machine: "A value that is not secret, such as a base URL or a path, should have a default".
explanation.c: Ruled out because moving the entry does not give the variable a value in Claude Code's own environment, and the documented answer is a default: "The documentation's answer is a default such as `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}`".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4, a developer-productivity agent. The agent explores unfamiliar codebases with the built-in tools and several MCP servers. A CI job runs `claude -p` on a fresh clone, and a pull request has added a server to `.mcp.json` that nobody on the team has seen. What happens when the job starts?

options.a: It stays pending until a person approves it in an interactive session
options.b: It is skipped, because an unattended run has no trust dialog to accept
options.c: It loads with no prompt, so edits to the file need the same review as source changes
options.d: It loads only if the repository's own settings file approves it in advance

explanation.c: Unattended runs cannot show the approval prompt.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the prompt needs a person: "In `claude -p` runs, Agent SDK sessions, and cloud sessions, Claude Code can't show that prompt: it loads project-scoped servers without asking."
explanation.b: is ruled out by the same sentence, which says such a run loads project-scoped servers and does not skip them: "it loads project-scoped servers without asking".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "approvals committed to the project's `.claude/settings.json` are ignored in a folder you have not trusted".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1, a customer support resolution agent. The agent's backend tools come from twelve MCP servers listed in the shared file, and sessions start with crowded context. A developer reads that tools from all servers are available simultaneously and marks all twelve servers `alwaysLoad`. What is the effect?

options.a: Startup waits without limit for the servers to connect
options.b: All their definitions return to the prompt at launch, undoing deferral
options.c: Only the tools that the first request needs are loaded, the rest later
options.d: Each tool gets the name of its server added so that names stay unique

explanation.b: `alwaysLoad` brings every definition into the initial context.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the wait is bounded: "capped at the standard 5-second connect timeout".
explanation.c: Ruled out because loading only what a request needs is what tool search does, and the flag turns that off: "Putting it on every server defeats tool search."
explanation.d: Ruled out because naming already carries the server: "a tool is called `mcp__<server>__<tool>`".
